nodes.description: Reduced or defective Sec61 channel limits the cotranslational transport of signal-peptide-bearing secretory and membrane proteins into the endoplasmic reticulum. Substrates differ in their sensitivity: in cellular models of the kidney variants, transport of renin was impaired, and the polycystic liver variant reduced polycystin-2 biosynthesis. Substrate selectivity is a proposed reason why different variants give different clinical presentations.

nodes.description: Germline heterozygous missense and nonsense variants in SEC61A1. Missense variants in the plug and pore ring regions (p.Val67Gly, p.Thr185Ala, p.Val85Asp, p.Gln92Arg) reduce protein stability or mislocalize the protein to the Golgi; the nonsense variant p.Glu381* acts by haploinsufficiency. Some missense variants are proposed to act in a dominant-negative way on calcium leak, so the net effect is a functional haploinsufficiency of the translocon.

nodes.description: Renin is a signal-peptide-dependent secretory protein made by the granular cells of the juxtaglomerular apparatus. The kidney variants impair its translocation in cellular models, and a patient biopsy lacked renin staining in juxtaglomerular cells. Low renin and aldosterone explain the hyperkalemia and hypotension seen in some patients, which corrected with a mineralocorticoid. The chemical chaperone phenylbutyrate restored renin transport in cellular models, but has not been tested in patients.

nodes.description: The open Sec61 channel is permeable to calcium and is a passive leak pathway from the endoplasmic reticulum to the cytosol. Patient variants in the pore ring and plug increase this leak, and cellular models of the kidney variants show reduced SERCA2. The resulting imbalance in endoplasmic reticulum calcium is one of the two proposed routes to endoplasmic reticulum stress.
